original_question: If a graph cocycle γ generates the formal flow P(ε)=exp(ε O→r(γ)(P)·∂/∂P⃗)P|_{ε=0} on Poisson bi-vectors, does that graph-defined power series converge and determine a globally well-defined Poisson structure at every point of an arbitrary affine Poisson manifold?
target_in_paper: Conjecture 1.1 in Section 1, read together with the local reparametrization interpretation supplied by Proposition 1.2 and the nearby globalization context in Theorem 1.3.
correct_elements: The draft correctly identifies the paper's analytic/integrability theme: a graph cocycle gamma induces an infinitesimal deformation of Poisson bi-vectors, and the question is whether the resulting formal flow has genuine geometric meaning on affine Poisson manifolds. It also correctly keeps the setting at the level of affine Poisson manifolds and focuses on convergence and well-definedness rather than on unrelated graph-combinatorial issues.
missing_details: The paper works with finite-dimensional real affine manifolds, not arbitrary Poisson manifolds without the affine restriction.
The graph datum must be specified as a cocycle gamma in Kontsevich's unoriented graph complex; nearby context treats cocycles whose summands have n vertices and 2n-2 edges.
The infinitesimal symmetry is the induced Poisson cocycle Q(P)=Or(gamma)(P^{\otimes n}), not an arbitrary graph-defined series.

The deformation is posed as the evolution equation dP/d\varepsilon = Q(P) with initial condition P|_{\varepsilon=0}=P; the draft's exponential notation hides this and incorrectly writes evaluation at \varepsilon=0 after exponentiation.
The relevant question is local in the deformation parameter (small \varepsilon), whereas the draft sounds like a global-in-time completeness question.

The nearby paper context distinguishes formal existence from geometric realization: if Q(P)=[[X,P]] is Poisson-exact, Proposition 1.2 interprets the deformation as an infinitesimal reparametrization/diffeomorphism.
The draft does not state that P is assumed Poisson, i.e. [[P,P]]=0, and that Q(P) is an infinitesimal symmetry of the Jacobi identity.
The draft omits the smooth-function ambient algebra C^\infty(M) and the Schouten bracket notation [[.,.]] that define Poisson cohomology and exactness in the paper's formulation.
The phrase 'globally well-defined Poisson structure at every point' is broader than the paper-faithful local-flow question suggested by Conjecture 1.1 and the immediately following Proposition 1.2.
No homogeneity, degree, or nilpotency hypothesis belongs to the targeted Conjecture 1.1 itself; those belong to a later specialized result, so they should not be inserted here.
refined_question: Let M be a finite-dimensional real affine manifold, let P be a Poisson bi-vector on M, and let gamma be a cocycle in Kontsevich's unoriented graph complex, inducing the infinitesimal Poisson symmetry Q(P)=Or(gamma)(P^{\otimes n}). Does the deformation equation dP/d\varepsilon = Q(P), with P|_{\varepsilon=0}=P, define a convergent local flow in \varepsilon on the space of Poisson bi-vectors on M; and, in the Poisson-exact case Q(P)=[[X,P]], is this flow realized geometrically by a local one-parameter family of reparametrizations/diffeomorphisms of the affine manifold rather than only as a formal power series?
justification: Your draft is closest to the paper's opening analytic/integrability problem, formally stated as Conjecture 1.1. The nearby context matters: Proposition 1.2 explains what an exact cocycle Q(P)=[[X,P]] means geometrically, namely an infinitesimal reparametrization of the underlying manifold, and Theorem 1.3 supplies the neighboring globalization perspective. So the stand-alone question should be phrased as a local-in-\varepsilon deformation problem for the induced cocycle Q(P)=Or(gamma)(P^{\otimes n}) on finite-dimensional real affine Poisson manifolds, not as an unrestricted global-time convergence question for an arbitrary graph-defined series.

citations.label: opening discussion of analytic/integrability and geometric meaning of graph flows
